source.title: [P0] Persist catalog, orders, inventory, reservations, and movement journal
source.body:
## Goal

Replace process-local business state with PostgreSQL as the durable system of record for the core Order and Inventory domains.

This issue establishes the storage foundation. Transactional correctness under concurrency is specified separately in the follow-up issue for atomic inventory operations.

## Scope

- Add PostgreSQL configuration and repeatable schema migrations.
- Introduce persistence/repository boundaries for:
  - products and catalog status;
  - orders and business outcomes;
  - inventory balances;
  - reservation records and lifecycle state;
  - append-only inventory movement journal;
  - idempotency records/results.
- Preserve the existing API contracts unless an explicit versioned change is required.
- Keep unit tests independent of a running PostgreSQL instance where practical, while adding real PostgreSQL integration tests.
- Define a deterministic development/test bootstrap for the existing demo catalog and inventory.

## Design constraints

- PostgreSQL owns business state; the Event Collector and dbt dataset are not sources of truth.
- The movement journal is a durable domain audit record, not a claim of full event sourcing.
- Inventory balances remain an operational projection and must be reconcilable against movements.
- Do not introduce multiple databases or a distributed database abstraction without a demonstrated need.
- Do not silently fall back to in-memory persistence in a production configuration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PostgreSQL schema and migration workflow are committed and reproducible from an empty database.
- [ ] Products, orders, balances, reservations, movement records, and idempotency results survive API process restarts.
- [ ] Repository implementations are used by the Order and Inventory services; business rules remain outside SQL-specific code.
- [ ] Movement records are append-only through the application interface.
- [ ] A consistency check can compare the current balance with the movement journal for a product.
- [ ] Demo/test seed data is explicit and deterministic; production startup does not silently seed business inventory.
- [ ] Integration tests exercise create/read/update/restart behavior against PostgreSQL.
- [ ] README documents configuration, migration, reset, and local development workflows.

## Out of scope

- Multi-region replication, sharding, or a production high-availability topology.
- Transactional outbox delivery (tracked separately).
- Supplier policy and purchase-order persistence (tracked separately).

## Priority

P0: core business state must survive restart before the application can claim durable operation.
